title: SAP’s cloud is still booming, and that was enough to calm the AI-doom fears
excerpt: SAP gave investors the number they wanted. Europe’s biggest software company said cloud revenue grew 22% to €6.28 billion in the second quarter, beating forecasts, SAP announced. Its cloud backlog, a measure of future sales, jumped 26%. The stock rose more than 6% in Frankfurt. That relief is the story. SAP’s shares are down about […]
content_html:
SAP gave investors the number they wanted. Europe’s biggest software company said cloud revenue grew 22% to €6.28 billion in the second quarter, beating forecasts, SAP announced. Its cloud backlog, a measure of future sales, jumped 26%. The stock rose more than 6% in Frankfurt.

That relief is the story. SAP’s shares are down about 35% this year, Bloomberg reported, on fears that AI will hollow out the enterprise-software subscription model SAP is built on. It reported in a jittery week of tech earnings. A strong cloud quarter is the clearest answer SAP can give: its customers are still signing up, not walking away.

A beat, and a guidance cut

The picture was not all rosy. Operating profit rose 7% to €2.74 billion, but missed analyst hopes. SAP also trimmed its 2026 profit outlook to €11.8-12.2 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported. The cut reflects the cost of two July acquisitions: the data firm Dremio and the AI startup Prior Labs.

SAP is spending hard to keep up. Chief executive Christian Klein has diverted budget and reshuffled management to fund an AI push, and the company cut hiring and travel to pay for it. It is pushing customers off older on-premise software and into the cloud. It will soon charge more to maintain legacy systems.

The AI story investors aren’t sold on

The bigger question is whether SAP’s own AI is any good. Klein casts it as an “Autonomous Enterprise” that grounds AI in a company’s core data. But some customers have questioned the value of SAP’s early AI tools, and analysts are lukewarm. “SAP still needs to do more to make its AI story compelling,” said Rebecca Wettemann of Valoir. “All its software running on the same platform isn’t a compelling reason to run enterprise AI there.”

So the quarter cuts both ways. The cloud numbers say AI has not broken SAP’s business, and investors were glad to hear it. But SAP has not yet shown that AI will grow it either, even as it spends to fend off rivals like Anthropic. For now, “we are not the disruption’s victim” was enough.

content_html_zh:
SAP 给了投资者他们想要的数字。 SAP 宣布，这家欧洲最大的软件公司表示，第二季度云收入增长 22%，达到 62.8 亿欧元，超出预期。 其云积压订单（衡量未来销售额的指标）跃升了 26%。 该股在法兰克福上涨超过 6%。

这种解脱就是故事。 据彭博社报道，由于担心人工智能将掏空 SAP 所建立的企业软件订阅模式，SAP 的股价今年下跌了约 35%。 该公司公布了令人紧张的一周科技财报。 强劲的云季度表现是 SAP 能够给出的最明确的答案：其客户仍在签约，而不是离开。

节拍和指导剪辑

情况并非一帆风顺。 营业利润增长 7% 至 27.4 亿欧元，但未达到分析师预期。 据《华尔街日报》报道，SAP 还将 2026 年利润预期下调至 11.8-122 亿欧元。 此次削减反映了 7 月份两项收购的成本：数据公司 Dremio 和人工智能初创公司 Prior Labs。

SAP 正在大力投入以跟上这一步伐。 首席执行官克里斯蒂安·克莱因(Christian Klein)转移了预算并改组了管理层，以资助人工智能的发展，公司还削减了招聘和差旅费用来支付费用。 它正在推动客户摆脱旧的本地软件并转向云。 它将很快收取更多费用来维护遗留系统。

投资者并不认同人工智能的故事

更大的问题是 SAP 自己的人工智能是否有任何好处。 克莱因将其视为一家“自主企业”，将人工智能植根于公司的核心数据中。 但一些客户质疑 SAP 早期人工智能工具的价值，分析师对此也态度冷淡。 Valoir 的丽贝卡·韦特曼 (Rebecca Wettemann) 表示：“SAP 仍需要采取更多措施，使其人工智能故事引人注目。” “所有在同一平台上运行的软件并不是在那里运行企业人工智能的令人信服的理由。”

因此，本季度是双向的。 云数据表明人工智能并未破坏 SAP 的业务，投资者很高兴听到这一消息。 但 SAP 还没有表明人工智能会推动它的发展，尽管它花费了大量资金来抵御 Anthropic 等竞争对手。 目前，“我们不是破坏的受害者”就足够了。
